commonsForms.name: Knowledge commons
commonsForms.definition: A shared knowledge resource system whose community, rules, resource characteristics, interactions, and outcomes can be analyzed together.

commonsForms.name: Information commons
commonsForms.definition: An information resource or environment organized for shared access, use, contribution, or stewardship.

commonsForms.name: Intellectual commons
commonsForms.definition: A shared domain for the creation, exchange, and reuse of intellectual work.

commonsForms.name: Scholarly communication commons
commonsForms.definition: Shared infrastructures, norms, repositories, and publication systems for scholarly communication.

commonsForms.name: Digital commons
commonsForms.definition: A commons whose resources, access facilities, and participation are substantially digital and networked.

commonsForms.name: Open-access commons
commonsForms.definition: A knowledge commons organized around free online access and permissions broad enough for scholarly use.

commonsForms.name: Scientific or research commons
commonsForms.definition: Shared scientific literature, data, models, tools, or collaborative infrastructure supporting research.

commonsForms.name: Cultural commons
commonsForms.definition: Shared cultural works, heritage materials, archives, and the institutions or rules sustaining access to them.

commonsForms.name: Civic knowledge commons
commonsForms.definition: A participatory civic resource through which residents, students, or organizations create and use public knowledge.

commonsForms.name: Learning commons
commonsForms.definition: A shared educational environment combining information resources, technology, instruction, and collaborative learning.

commonsForms.name: Community information commons
commonsForms.definition: A community-facing information environment that supports local access, deliberation, contribution, and public problem solving.

commonsForms.name: Digital library
commonsForms.definition: A managed digital collection with discovery, access, organization, and often preservation services.

commonsForms.name: Digital archive
commonsForms.definition: A managed body of digital objects maintained across time with provenance, authenticity, or preservation responsibilities.

commonsForms.name: Institutional repository
commonsForms.definition: A repository organized by an institution to collect, expose, and often preserve its community's scholarly output.

commonsForms.name: Disciplinary repository
commonsForms.definition: A repository organized around a discipline or research community rather than one institution.

commonsForms.name: Epistemic repository
commonsForms.definition: A repository designed around a community's structured knowledge, concepts, evidence, and reusable research objects.

commonsForms.name: Specialist archive
commonsForms.definition: A focused archive built for a specialist scholarly field, corpus, format, or community.

commonsForms.name: Community-based archive
commonsForms.definition: An archive shaped and maintained with direct participation by the community represented in its holdings.

commonsForms.name: Author self-archive
commonsForms.definition: A repository or site through which authors deposit and expose their own work.

commonsForms.name: Open educational resource library
commonsForms.definition: A collection or gateway providing openly accessible teaching and learning materials.

commonsForms.name: Searchable portal
commonsForms.definition: A central discovery interface that searches or organizes resources held locally and elsewhere.

commonsForms.name: Annotated link gateway
commonsForms.definition: A link-only gateway that points to off-site resources and adds classification metadata and descriptive context.

commonsForms.name: Metadata aggregation or harvesting service
commonsForms.definition: A service that collects standardized metadata from distributed repositories to support shared discovery.

commonsForms.name: Directory or registry
commonsForms.definition: A structured listing of projects, repositories, policies, people, resources, or implementations.

commonsForms.name: Open-access journal
commonsForms.definition: A journal that makes its articles freely accessible online under an open-access delivery model.

commonsForms.name: Open publication platform
commonsForms.definition: A shared service for publishing, reviewing, distributing, or linking scholarly works outside a conventional closed journal system.

commonsForms.name: Free/libre and open-source software commons
commonsForms.definition: A software project whose code, participation rules, licenses, and collaborative production constitute a commons.

commonsForms.name: Open-content science commons
commonsForms.definition: A proposed or operating science commons applying open-source participation, review, licensing, and versioning to scientific content.

commonsForms.name: Scientific data commons
commonsForms.definition: Shared infrastructure for depositing, accessing, documenting, and reusing scientific datasets.

commonsForms.name: Collaboratory
commonsForms.definition: A networked environment in which geographically distributed participants share data, instruments, tools, and research work.

commonsForms.name: Information community
commonsForms.definition: A community joined by shared information practices, resources, tools, standards, and stewardship.

commonsForms.name: Federated or distributed library
commonsForms.definition: Multiple independent repositories or institutions connected through shared protocols, services, or discovery layers.

commonsForms.name: Coalition or membership network
commonsForms.definition: A network of institutions or projects coordinating access, policy, preservation, standards, or advocacy.

commonsForms.name: Organizational archive
commonsForms.definition: An archive housed within the same organization as either the producer or consumer, or contracted to a third party.

commonsForms.name: Producer archive
commonsForms.definition: An archive maintained by the organization or person producing the content.

commonsForms.name: Consumer archive
commonsForms.definition: An archive maintained by the institution or community consuming and relying on the content.

commonsForms.name: Independent third-party archive
commonsForms.definition: A preservation archive institutionally separate from both producer and consumer.

commonsForms.name: Distributed preservation network
commonsForms.definition: A preservation arrangement using redundant, distributed copies or caches across participating institutions.

commonsForms.name: Dark archive or fallback-access archive
commonsForms.definition: A preservation service whose stored materials become accessible only under defined loss, trigger, or continuity conditions.

commonsForms.name: Open licensing infrastructure
commonsForms.definition: Licenses, registries, declarations, or policy services that define reusable permissions for knowledge resources.

commonsForms.name: Standards and interoperability infrastructure
commonsForms.definition: Shared metadata, identifiers, protocols, interfaces, and technical rules that let independent commons interoperate.

commonsForms.name: Traditional natural-resource commons
commonsForms.definition: Shared forests, fisheries, pastures, water systems, and other subtractable resources used as the analytical starting point for knowledge commons.

commonsForms.name: Public domain
commonsForms.directoryRole: Legal status and surrounding resource pool
commonsForms.definition: Knowledge and cultural material available outside exclusive copyright control, serving as a key resource environment for commons projects.

projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: The book's baseline access institution, governed by first sale, preservation, and public-service norms.

projectTypes.name: diffuse library
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A library whose content, expertise, and access functions are distributed beyond one building or collection.

projectTypes.name: digital library
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A managed digital collection joined to discovery, access, preservation, and user services.

projectTypes.name: collaborative or federated digital library
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: Multiple institutions coordinate collections, protocols, and governance to provide a shared service.

projectTypes.name: digital collection
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A coherent set of digitized or born-digital objects presented as a reusable corpus.
representativeEntries: Library of Congress Edison film collection

projectTypes.name: national library and catalog
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: National-scale holdings, catalogs, and preservation coordination.

projectTypes.name: institutional repository
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: An institutionally managed archive for faculty and organizational scholarship.

projectTypes.name: disciplinary repository
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A repository shared by a discipline rather than one institution.

projectTypes.name: epistemic repository
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A repository whose resource units are claims, artifacts, and community validation processes.

projectTypes.name: personal or self-archive
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: An author's own website or deposit route for openly circulating scholarship.

projectTypes.name: organizational archive
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: An archive operated by the organization that creates or controls the content; preservation Model A or B.

projectTypes.name: producer archive
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: An archive run by content producers or their institutions; preservation Model C.

projectTypes.name: consumer archive
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: An archive maintained by consumers or subscribing libraries; preservation Model D.

projectTypes.name: community-based or trusted third-party archive
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A collectively trusted independent preservation service; preservation Model E.

projectTypes.name: dark or restricted preservation archive
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: An archive that preserves content but releases it only under specified trigger conditions.

projectTypes.name: specialist archive
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A narrowly focused collection assembled by a specialist or community rather than a universal institution.

projectTypes.name: web archive
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A preservation collection capturing portions of the changing web.

projectTypes.name: repository network or federation
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: Interoperable repositories whose metadata and holdings form a larger distributed corpus.
representativeEntries: Networked Digital Library of Theses and Dissertations

projectTypes.name: campus information commons

projectTypes.name: campus learning commons
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A learner-centered facility and program organized around shared learning tasks.

projectTypes.name: portal, directory, bibliography, or reference guide
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A curated discovery structure pointing users to distributed resources, policies, or concepts.

projectTypes.name: open-access journal
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A peer-reviewed journal whose articles are freely available online.

projectTypes.name: open-access publisher or journal platform
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: An organization or platform that publishes and distributes OA journals.

projectTypes.name: dynamic or compound publication environment
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A publication designed for continual revision or combining journal, alerts, dialogue, data, and analytic tools.

projectTypes.name: library publishing service
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A library unit supplying publication technology, production, and stewardship.

projectTypes.name: information community
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: An integrated digital setting joining a community's resources, tools, activities, and participants.

projectTypes.name: collaboratory
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: An online environment for remote instrument use, data analysis, communication, and research preservation.

projectTypes.name: virtual laboratory
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A networked setting in which distributed participants configure, run, and analyze experiments.

projectTypes.name: data archive or research database
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A maintained corpus of empirical data for analysis, teaching, or civic research.

projectTypes.name: open educational resource
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: Course, book, handbook, experiment, or learning content made openly usable.

projectTypes.name: civic research and mapping project
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: Community-university work translating local data into public maps, indicators, deliberation, and action.

projectTypes.name: distributed preservation system
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: Replicated, coordinated storage designed to keep digital materials available despite local failure.

projectTypes.name: trusted third-party preservation service
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: An independent organization preserving publishers' source files under agreed access triggers.

projectTypes.name: national digital-preservation program
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A national plan or program coordinating distributed custody, standards, and stewardship.
representativeEntries: National Digital Information and Infrastructure Preservation Program

projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: Shared metadata, vocabularies, and relationship structures that make heterogeneous collections work together.

projectTypes.name: repository software

projectTypes.name: content-management and journal-workflow software

projectTypes.name: version-control infrastructure
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: Tools that track contributions, branches, and versions in distributed collaborative production.

projectTypes.name: open-source project-hosting platform
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: Shared infrastructure for hosting source, versions, issue discussion, and developer coordination.

projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A standardized permission instrument allowing specified reuse of creative and knowledge works.

projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A license granting source access and reuse rights, sometimes requiring derivatives to remain open.

projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: Administrative machinery for registering exclusive rights or reducing permission transaction costs.
